_description: Scenarios for Lab 13. 'indicators' are the analyst's structured observations (keys of config threat_classification.actors / motivation_rules); 'initial_access' is the observed entry vector (key of threat_classification.vectors).

scenarios.title: Quiet theft at a defense contractor
scenarios.narrative: Engineers at a defense contractor visited a compromised industry-news site. Custom malware, never seen before, stayed hidden for nine months while design documents trickled out to infrastructure linked to a foreign government.

scenarios.title: Hospital ransomware
scenarios.narrative: A billing clerk opened an invoice email. Within hours file servers were encrypted, and a note demanded 40 BTC for the decryption key.

scenarios.title: City website defaced
scenarios.narrative: The day after a controversial council vote, the city website showed a protest banner and went down under a DDoS. A group claimed responsibility on social media. Entry was through an unpatched CMS plugin.

scenarios.title: Backups wiped by an administrator
scenarios.narrative: A systems administrator passed over for promotion logged in at 2 a.m. with his own credentials and deleted the backup catalogs.

scenarios.title: Lobby cameras hijacked
scenarios.narrative: A teenager ran a free scanning tool, logged into lobby IP cameras still using admin/admin, and posted screenshots online for clout. The traffic was loud and obvious.

scenarios.title: Customer list on a public share
scenarios.narrative: The marketing team signed up for an unapproved file-sharing service to move large files and left a link public. Nobody meant any harm.

scenarios.title: USB sticks in the parking lot
scenarios.narrative: Branded USB sticks were left in a clinic parking lot. One was plugged in; patient records later appeared for sale on a dark-web market.

scenarios.title: Executive mailbox extortion
scenarios.narrative: A caller impersonating the CFO talked the help desk into resetting MFA. Days later the attackers sent samples of the CFO's emails: pay, or everything gets published.
